name: Taurifer UI screen catalog
description: Every user-visible mobile surface, captured from the production UI. Onboarding is covered state by state so no route is represented only by its first screen.

intentionalScrollers.reason: Muscle filters retain a partially visible final chip as a horizontal continuation cue.
Equipment filters retain a partially visible final chip as a horizontal continuation cue.

nonOverlapGroups.reason: The two filter rails and their visible chips may continue off-edge but must not cover one another.

screens.label: One-time landing
screens.scenario: First empty visit. The hero: headline, subtitle, the Build pill, the Track link, three chips and Privacy, with the device-local seen state. The bands below it have their own scrolled states.

screens.label: One-time landing — proof
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the proof: seven steps over the real workout screen with the pinned phone, lens and rail, and the persistent Build control.

screens.label: One-time landing — three ways
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the three ways to start your training: the orange, surface and ink stripes, with the paste hand-off closed.

screens.label: One-time landing — outcomes
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the three engine outcomes (add, hold, back off) with their next targets, and the strength-trend chart.

screens.label: One-time landing — your data
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the ink band: the history stays on the phone, in three rows.

screens.label: One-time landing — questions
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the questions with the RIR answer open.

screens.label: One-time landing — close
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the closing orange band with the Build pill and the Track link; the persistent Build control has stepped aside.

screens.label: Returning landing
screens.scenario: A later visit to a device with no program and no log, with nothing saved. The welcome-back headline and its line, the Build pill, the Track link and Privacy lead; the chips, the proof and the outcomes are left out, and the ways, the data promise, the questions and the closing band follow.

screens.label: Returning landing — setup saved
screens.scenario: A later visit with a half-finished Recommend setup saved. The lead action names it (Continue choosing your program) in the hero and the closing band; tapping it opens the chooser's resume card.

screens.label: Entry hub
screens.scenario: B's hub: Recommend, Build and Import as choice cards, the setup-link note, Continue held until a choice.

screens.label: Entry hub — guide
screens.scenario: The entry guide over the hub: the guide dialog, centred over the dimmed hub.

screens.label: Entry hub — Recommend chosen
screens.scenario: The hub with Recommend chosen and Continue enabled.

screens.label: Entry hub — existing program
screens.scenario: Opened from Settings while a program is active, so replacement consequences are in view.

screens.label: Recommend — building
screens.scenario: B's third checklist line is active after two lines complete, with generation still in the real worker and Show the program now available.

screens.label: Recommend — waiting for generation
screens.scenario: With reduced motion, B's checklist is complete and the real worker request remains pending with its waiting label visible.

screens.label: Recommend — recommendation and review
screens.scenario: Onboarding B's review editor at rest: the source, the program name, four facts, the block row and its Change action, the day tabs with rest days and the first day's exercises with their sets, RIR and muscles; how it was built follows, with the pinned activation.

screens.label: Recommend — offered movement
screens.scenario: A real Worker-verified movement offer under its current exercise row, with the approved advice and confirmation action.

screens.label: Recommend — confirmed movement
screens.scenario: After confirming the offered movement: its row is marked Confirmed by you, Undo is available, and the changed rows are announced.

screens.label: Recommend — block inputs
screens.scenario: The result's block sheet with seven regular weeks and the undulating rep pattern selected; the additional deload is off after exercising its switch.

screens.label: Recommend — equipment conflict
screens.scenario: The result explains that the available candidates cannot complete the program, says nothing was saved, and offers Back to equipment with the adjustment preserved.

screens.label: Recommend — review with adjustments
screens.scenario: Three rows carry their marks (a set added, an engine swap, a movement added from the catalog) and the changes bar counts them with Undo and Restore.

screens.label: Recommend — exercise sheet
screens.scenario: One exercise's sheet at its top: the movement, its role and job, the sets ledger with RIR per set, the set count, rep range and rest controls, and the day's time.

screens.label: Recommend — execution mode
screens.scenario: The exercise sheet asks how an ambiguous per-side movement is performed, with both approved answers and the unresolved Review cue.

screens.label: Recommend — swap and alternates
screens.scenario: The exercise sheet scrolled to the engine's swap candidates, the catalog search and one in-session alternate with its suggestions.

screens.label: Recommend — day actions
screens.scenario: The day menu sheet: rename the day, reorder its exercises, add an exercise.

screens.label: Recommend — duplicate day name refused
screens.scenario: The day rename sheet keeps a duplicate name in the field and shows the existing linked alert.

screens.label: Recommend — reorder a day
screens.scenario: A day in reorder mode: each exercise with its handle and up and down arrows, and Done.

screens.label: Recommend — an emptied day
screens.scenario: Every exercise of a training day removed: the tab's pip, the day's warning with Add exercise, and Activate disabled with its reason.

screens.label: Recommend — rebuild asks first
screens.scenario: An answer chip would rebuild an adjusted program: the confirmation to rebuild or keep the adjustments.

screens.label: Recommend — recommendation with a program active
screens.scenario: The merged candidate surface while the current program remains untouched.

screens.label: Recommend — answer editor open
screens.scenario: The review with the days-per-week chip open on its inline editor: the same numeric cards as the question, an Update program action, and the pinned activation set aside.

screens.label: Recommend — after a changed answer
screens.scenario: A changed answer rebuilt the program in place: the change statement with Before and Now, an added exercise tagged new, and its day open.

screens.label: Recommend — after avoiding an exercise
screens.scenario: An exercise the program contained is avoided from the priorities editor: the statement, and the constraint line with Restore.

screens.label: Recommend — confirm replacement
screens.scenario: The explicit archive-and-replace confirmation. History is not changed.

screens.label: Recommend — activation conflict
screens.scenario: Another tab changed the active program. The newer program stays active.

screens.label: Build 1 — name and days
screens.scenario: The build_setup step: program name and day count before the editor opens.

screens.label: Build — empty days
screens.scenario: Real empty day containers, Add exercise, Save draft, activation disabled.

screens.label: Build — partial draft
screens.scenario: One populated day and one incomplete day. Activation stays disabled.

screens.label: Build — activation ready
screens.scenario: A complete manual draft with supported progression and activation enabled.

screens.label: Build — editor alternates
screens.scenario: The Build editor (the classic layout) with its first exercise's in-session alternates: two chosen movements in order, each with move and remove controls, and Add alternate.

screens.label: Import — source
screens.scenario: Import's first screen: Choose file and Paste a program, each with its explanation, and the way out to Build, before any mutation.

screens.label: Import — paste a program
screens.scenario: The free-form door as it opens: an empty field, and the hand-off to ChatGPT or Claude still unavailable.

screens.label: Import — paste ready to convert
screens.scenario: A pasted program with both app links live, the character counter, and the field the reply comes back into.

screens.label: Import — choose an assistant
screens.scenario: Stage 2 with collapsed source summary, Edit button, ChatGPT and Claude buttons, and Preview prompt disclosure.

screens.label: Import — paste reply
screens.scenario: Stage 3 with collapsed source summary, Import from clipboard, the "or paste" divider, reply textarea, Review CTA, Try another assistant, and Start over.

screens.label: Import — resolve gaps
screens.scenario: Gap resolution screen with inputs for missing sets and reps, and the non-imported disclosure.

screens.label: Import — gap validation error
screens.scenario: Gap resolution screen after submitting empty inputs, highlighting invalid fields with .is-invalid and aria-invalid.

screens.label: Import — unreadable reply
screens.scenario: Unreadable reply recovery block with Copy repair prompt and Try another assistant actions.

screens.label: Import — exercise review
screens.scenario: Reviewing candidate matches: collapsed candidate chips, disclosure expanded, and unmatched flat escape hatches.

screens.label: Import — review
screens.scenario: A mapped exercise with manual progression ownership and provenance.

screens.label: Shared setup — adaptive landing
screens.scenario: The received-program gate names its program and training days, shows the no-history/no-change disclosure, and offers See the program plus Create a program from scratch.

screens.label: Shared setup — invalid landing
screens.scenario: An invalid setup link explains that nothing was saved and keeps safe Build and Track actions available.

screens.label: Shared setup — review
screens.scenario: The received program in B's review with the Shared program source, Restore, and its block as received (no Change), before explicit activation.

screens.label: Resume setup
screens.scenario: The resumable notice after reload: route, step, recency, Resume, Start over.

screens.label: Rules changed
screens.scenario: A draft whose compiler rules are stale. Rebuild is required before activation.

screens.label: Cancel setup — keep or discard
screens.scenario: Cancel pressed mid-flow. A dialog over the current step asks whether to keep the draft or discard it; Escape or Continue setup returns to the step.

screens.label: Start over — confirm
screens.scenario: Start over pressed on a review. A dialog asks before the answers and the unused program are discarded; the active program does not change.

screens.label: Today — no program
screens.scenario: A fresh device after leaving setup, with no program or workout controls.

screens.label: Today — ready to start
screens.scenario: The Direction D lifter before Day 1 starts: the prescription table reads recommendation() for every exercise, with the verdict tally above it.

screens.label: Today — dock large-content viewer
screens.scenario: A finger holds the dock's Progress tab. At 200% text the large-content viewer shows its icon and name large over Today, which keeps its one-row dock with capped labels; at the usual size (the canonical frame) the labels are whole, so the hold is only a press and no viewer is offered.

screens.label: Today — ready to start, scrolled
screens.scenario: Plan 075 phase 3: the same ready state, scrolled past the large title, so the scroll-edge bar's material and its mirrored inline title are showing.

screens.scenario: The rest countdown remains visible after leaving the active workout.

screens.label: Today — choose another day
screens.scenario: The day picker sheet open.

screens.label: Workout — focus mode
screens.scenario: One exercise at a time.

screens.label: Workout — first-set guide

screens.scenario: The focus-utilities guide: the guide dialog centred over the dimmed Focus.

screens.scenario: The per-exercise note sheet.

screens.scenario: A second tap on the selected Reps field opens the wheel, 1 to 30, with the prescription's target range marked on the rail.

screens.label: Workout — why this weight

screens.label: Session summary — declined

screens.label: Session summary — first session
